text: CSMT was designed by F. W. Stevens and completed in 1888; it was formerly known as Victoria Terminus.
CSMT blends Victorian Gothic Revival with Indian architectural traditions and was inscribed as a UNESCO World Heritage Site in 2004.
The Gateway of India commemorates the 1911 visit of King George V and Queen Mary; it was designed by George Wittet and completed in 1924.
Flora Fountain stands at a junction officially called Hutatma Chowk, in memory of those who died in the Samyukta Maharashtra movement.
The Bombay High Court building is Gothic Revival in style and was completed in 1878.
The Rajabai Clock Tower was designed by George Gilbert Scott, completed in 1878, and named after the mother of its donor, Premchand Roychand.
Kala Ghoda means 'black horse'; the area was named after a statue of Edward VII on horseback that was later moved away.
The CSMVS museum building opened in 1922 as the Prince of Wales Museum and was designed by George Wittet in the Indo-Saracenic style.
The David Sassoon Library was completed in 1870 and is built in the Gothic Revival style.
Horniman Circle was originally called Elphinstone Circle and was renamed after Benjamin Guy Horniman, editor of the Bombay Chronicle.
Crawford Market was completed in 1869 and designed by William Emerson; Lockwood Kipling contributed to its sculptural decoration.
Marine Drive is lined with Art Deco buildings from the 1930s and 40s; Mumbai's Victorian Gothic and Art Deco ensembles were inscribed by UNESCO in 2018.
Mahalaxmi Dhobi Ghat is a large open-air laundry where clothes are washed by hand in rows of stone wash pens.
Banganga Tank is a sacred tank beside the Walkeshwar temple area, traditionally dated to the 12th century.
Sassoon Dock was completed in 1875 and is a working fishing dock where catches are landed and sorted.
Britannia & Co., an Irani cafe in Ballard Estate, opened in 1923.
Mumbai's dabbawalas deliver home-cooked lunches to office workers using a system that dates back to the 1890s.
Mahim Nature Park was developed on a former dumping ground.
The Bandra-Worli Sea Link, opened in 2009, is a cable-stayed bridge across Mahim Bay.
The Fort area is named after the old Bombay Fort, and most of its walls were taken down in the 1860s.
